english.title: Throw an article / substance into a prison

english.notes:
(i) In proceedings for an offence under this section it is a defence for the accused to show that -
(a) he reasonably believed that he had authorisation to do the act in respect of which the proceedings are brought, or
(b) in all the circumstances there was an overriding public interest which justified the doing of that act.
(ii) Authorisation means authorisation given for the purposes of this section; and subsections (1) to (3) of section 40E apply in relation to authorisations so given as they apply to authorisations given for the purposes of section 40D.
(iii) The reference to an article or substance does not include a reference to a List A article, a List B article or a List C article (as defined by section 40A).
(iv) The reference to "throwing" an article or substance into a prison includes a reference to doing anything from outside the prison that results in the article or substance being projected or conveyed over or through a boundary of the prison so as to land inside the prison.

other.penalty:
Either waySummary: maximum 6/12 months imprisonment and/or a fine.
Indictment: maximum 2 years imprisonment and/or a fine.

The maximum penalty on summary conviction is 6 months for offences committed before 2nd May 2022; for offences committed on or after that date it may be 6 or 12 months depending on the general limit in a magistrates’ court, see paragraph 5 of Schedule 4 to the Offender Management Act 2007 and section 224(1) and (1A) of the Sentencing Act 2022.
